In summary, our research is concerned with
the physical and chemical processes that control the formation of molecular oxygen, a key species in the chemistry of interstellar space.
the physical conditions in a small region of Orion, where the O2 emission arises from a small, hot (T > 100 K), dense (n(H2) > 105 cm-3) source.
the physical and chemical processes that govern the structure of the interstellar medium and the formation of stars, planets, and life.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we do not know what the O2 is doing in Orion, but we know that it is doing something.
the observed O2 is produced in the warm (>= 100 K) dust in the Peak A region, which has a mass of ~10 M sun.
the Herschel observations of O2 are consistent with both the desorption of water ice and the shock excitation mechanisms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found a new source of oxygen gas in the interstellar medium (ISM).
the O2 abundance in Orion is not anomalous, and that the O2 column densities are not anomalous.
Herschel has provided a unique view of the Orion molecular cloud complex and its environment, and that the O2 data are a key part of this view.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can now measure the O2 column density in a small, dense region of the H2 peak 1 position in Orion.
the HIFI observations of O2 in the H2 peaks of Orion are the first direct detection of vibrationally excited H2O2 in the ISM and provide a new tool for studying gas-phase chemistry.
O2 is an excellent probe of warm, dense gas in Orion, but the interpretation of the line intensities is not yet clear.
